- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in first 2–3 days of sentiment reversal.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, true outcome often reverses or dips; apply mean reversion by reducing forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is flat or rising slowly, true outcome often shows volatility or downward correction; add 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
